| ASM-0513 | P10 publishes rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1 on rwb.agent.events.v1 (CloudEvents 1.0, key caseId) from the outbox in the same transaction as the run row, carrying runId, agent INTAKE, caseId, outcome and fallback and no personal value; rwb-decision, rwb-document and rwb-deviation consume it as the catalogue states. | The legacy story publishes EV-28 AgentRunCompleted after storing the run; the target keeps the event, gives it the P10 topic and requires the outbox fact in one transaction. | RWB-E1-059 sections 4 step 5, 7 AC1, 11 and 12; Arch v5 slides 16 (P10 OUT AgentRunCompleted), 20 (outbox in every service) and 43 (event 28 and its consumers); Ownership Map event EV-28 (P10); Template and Rules v1 sections R4 and R5.5 DP-09. | GAP-0369 | Story sections 4 step 5, 7 AC12, 12.3 and 12.4 | High | P10 agent owner and P7 decision owner | Exactly one event per run; a consumer can act on the run without a synchronous call to P10. | B-ITG-W1-08 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-0514 | The six document types and the LOV-DOC-TYPE codes in force are read through the P3 rwb-case reference-data contract (GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode} and the catalogue version), not through P4 rwb-access and not from a lov_value table; a type outside the list in force is scored as unknown and no proposal is made for it. | The legacy story takes LOV-DOC-TYPE through P4, while the table ruling and DP-07 put reference data and LOV with P3 rwb-case; the suite needs one named owner for the type list. | RWB-E1-060 sections 3, 4 step 7, 5 X1, 7 AC3, 11 and 13 (LOV-DOC-TYPE through P4); Template and Rules v1 sections R3 default ruling and R5.5 DP-07; Ownership Map tables lov_value, reference_row, reference_version (P3) and api row GET /admin/lists/{listCode} (P3). | GAP-0370 | Story sections 3, 4 step 7, 7 AC10, 11 and 12.2 | Medium | P3 case owner, P4 access owner and P10 agent owner | The type list still changes by a reference-data version without a release; the read moves to its owner. | B-ITG-W1-08 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-0515 | P5 rwb-document serves the document, its content and the stored fields to P10 through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}, GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/content and the field read behind GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents; the suite asserts a document_field value through the P5 contract and never reads the table. | The legacy story calls P5 DocumentQueryService.getFields and getContent inside the monolith; the target keeps document, content and field with P5 and the suite must prove the read across the boundary. | RWB-E1-060 sections 3, 4 steps 3 and 4, 7 AC1 and AC6, 11 (DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-017), 12 (DocumentQueryService) and 13; Arch v5 slide 16 (P5 IN and OUT); Ownership Map tables document, document_field (P5) and api rows GET /documents/{documentId}, GET /documents/{documentId}/content, GET /cases/{caseId}/documents (P5); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-01 and DP-11. | GAP-0370 | Story sections 3, 4 steps 3 to 5, 7 AC1, AC4, AC9 and AC14, 11 and 12.2 | High | P5 document owner and P10 agent owner | The OCR_TEMPLATE approach reads the same stored values as before; no copy of a field is held in rwb_agent. | B-ITG-W1-08 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-0516 | All three approaches run inside P10 rwb-agent: OCR_TEMPLATE reads the P5 stored fields only and makes no model call, while MODEL and OCR_AND_MODEL call agent EXTRACT in shadow through the P10 orchestrator to the recorded INT-23 stub; no service outside P10 calls the model endpoint and no live model endpoint is used in SIT. | The legacy story runs the three approaches inside the P10 module and calls the model through its gateway; the target keeps the evaluation and the gateway with P10, and the suite needs a deterministic stub for the timeout, tie and failure cases. | RWB-E1-060 sections 3, 4 steps 3 to 5, 5 X2, 7 AC1, AC4 and AC5, 8 BR6, 12 and 13; Arch v5 slide 16 (P10 IN and OUT, AgentRunWorkflow 60 s then rule result); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-11 and DP-20. | GAP-0370 | Story sections 3, 4, 7 AC4, AC5, AC9 and AC11, 12.8 and 17 | High | P10 agent owner and the Enterprise AI platform owner | The three approaches stay comparable on the same documents; the failure and tie paths are reproducible. | B-ITG-W1-08 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-0517 | The score rows and the proposal stay in P10 (agent_evaluation_run and agent_evaluation in rwb_agent), the proposal column is added by P10's own migration V10_003, and the export and the reads go through GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations with Accept text/csv for the proposal rows; the suite writes no evaluation table. | The legacy story adds the proposal column to agent_evaluation_run and reads and exports it through GET /admin/agent-evaluations; the target keeps the tables and the operation with P10 inside its own schema and Flyway sequence. | RWB-E1-060 sections 4 steps 6 to 8, 7 AC2, AC3, AC5 and AC7, 11 (DF-AGT-070 to DF-AGT-096), 12, 13 (V10_003__evaluation_proposal.sql) and 16; Ownership Map tables agent_evaluation_run and agent_evaluation (P10) and api row GET /admin/agent-evaluations (P10); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-15. | GAP-0370 | Story sections 4 steps 6 to 8, 7 AC1, AC2 and AC13, 12.2 and 12.7 | High | P10 agent owner | The proposal and its precision and recall stay readable per field and per type; no schema of another service is involved. | B-ITG-W1-08 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-0518 | The target precision 0.95, the minimum labeled sample 30 and the tie order stay values of agent_policy EXTRACT P1, loaded by RW-COE and approved by RW-RISK through the P10 admin contract; the evaluation changes no document_field value and no review threshold in force in P5, and the suite asserts both through the P5 contract before and after the run. | The legacy story holds the target precision, the sample floor and the tie order in the policy row and says the evaluation changes no field and no threshold; the target keeps them in P10 data and the no-change guardrail now crosses into P5. | RWB-E1-060 sections 3, 6, 7 AC2 and AC7, 8 BR3 to BR5, 13 and 17; Ownership Map tables agent_policy (P10), document_field (P5) and api rows GET and POST /admin/agent-configs (P10), GET /documents/{documentId} (P5); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-01 and DP-06. | GAP-0370 | Story sections 3, 7 AC2, AC7 and AC14, 8 BR3 to BR5, 12.2 and 13 | High | P10 agent owner, P5 document owner and the risk and model risk officer | A threshold change is still a P5 reference-data change after the measurement, and no value of the evaluation leaks into the live field set. | B-ITG-W1-08 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-0519 | P10 reads the interactions of a case through P1 rwb-source-data at GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions with the 180-day window and asserts occurred_at, channel and a masked summary; it does not call a P7 InteractionLedgerReader and reads no interaction table. | The legacy story reads the ledger through a P7 reader inside the monolith; the R-PREC default ruling and DP-18 put the interaction ledger with P1, and the case timeline stays with P3. | RWB-E1-062 sections 4 step 3, 7 AC5, 11 (DF-INT-001 to DF-INT-011) and 12 (P7 InteractionLedgerReader); Template and Rules v1 section R3 default ruling and R5.5 DP-18; Ownership Map tables interaction (P1) and api row GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions (P1). | GAP-0371 | Story sections 3, 4 step 3, 7 AC5 and AC10, 11 and 12.2 | Medium | P1 source data owner and P10 agent owner | The preceding contact is still found in the 30 days before the complaint, and the summary is masked before the model call. | B-ITG-W1-08 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-0520 | Rule rows R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 and the owner role of each code stay in P7 rwb-decision, and P10 evaluates the DEVIATIONS package with the embedded Drools kit (DP-04); the suite reads the package version in force through GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions and asserts the owner role on the proposal, because the Ownership Map lists no rule-row read operation for another service. | The legacy story calls a P3 RuleEvaluator.ownerFor and a RuleCatalog; the table ruling gives rule rows to P7, and DP-04 gives every service an embedded Drools kit with the package from rwb-decision. | RWB-E1-062 sections 3, 4 step 5, 5 X5, 7 AC4, 11 (DF-REF-002 and DF-REF-010) and 12 (RuleCatalog, RuleEvaluator.ownerFor); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-04; Ownership Map tables rule_row, rule_package, rule_package_version (P7) and api rows GET /admin/rule-packages, GET /admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions (P7). | GAP-0371 | Story sections 3, 4 step 5, 7 AC4 and AC11, 8 BR3, 12.2 and 12.5 | Medium | P7 decision owner and P10 agent owner | A rule change still moves a code to its owner without a release; the package version that produced the role is the one in force. | B-ITG-W1-08 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-0521 | The deviation codes X1 to X7 are read from the P3 rwb-case reference-data contract (GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}, list LOV-DEVIATION); no code is written in P10 or in the suite, and the run records the code list version in force. | The legacy story takes the codes from LOV-DEVIATION and requires the answer to hold a code in X1 to X7; the target keeps reference data with P3 under DP-07, so the list must be read from its owner. | RWB-E1-062 sections 3, 4 step 4, 5 X1, 7 AC8, 8 BR2, 11 and 13; Template and Rules v1 sections R3 default ruling and R5.5 DP-07; Ownership Map tables lov_value, reference_row, reference_version (P3) and api row GET /admin/lists/{listCode} (P3). | GAP-0371 | Story sections 3, 4 step 4, 7 AC8 and AC11, 8 BR2, 12.2 and 13 | High | P3 case owner and P10 agent owner | A new code is a reference-data version change, and a code outside the list fails the schema check exactly as before. | B-ITG-W1-08 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-0522 | P10 starts the screening run from EV-01 CaseCreated on rwb.case.events.v1 and EV-16 DocumentStored on rwb.document.events.v1 into its inbox, and runs AgentRunWorkflow on queue rwb-agent with the key SCREENING:<caseId>:<eventId>; in SHADOW mode it calls no S8 component and publishes no deviation event. | The legacy listener consumes EV-01 and EV-16 in process and states that nothing is raised in shadow; the target keeps the events, gives the run a workflow and queue, and leaves S8 untouched in shadow. | RWB-E1-062 sections 3, 4 steps 1 and 2, 5 X4, 7 AC3 and AC7, 12 (EV-01, EV-16, EV-28) and 13; Arch v5 slides 15 (S8 IN), 16 (P10 IN), 41, 42 (events 01 and 16) and 43 (event 28); Ownership Map events EV-01 (P3), EV-16 (P5), EV-28 (P10) and workflow AgentRunWorkflow (P10); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-09 and DP-20. | GAP-0371 | Story sections 3, 4 steps 1 and 2, 7 AC3, AC7, AC12 and AC15, 12.4 and 12.5 | High | P10 agent owner and S8 deviation owner | One run per case and event; a repeated event is absorbed by the inbox and the run key, and no deviation is raised in shadow. | B-ITG-W1-08 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |

| ASM-0549 | The chain-check Schedule decisionChainCheck lives in rwb-decision as JOB-14 at 02:00 Asia/Bangkok with overlap policy SKIP and a catch-up window, and its ChainCheckWorkflow checks the central ledger of rwb_decision and every wave-1 local decision_record chain it has ingested, from chain_seq 1 to the highest chain_seq at the start of each chain, in batches of 1,000, recomputing every entry_hash and comparing every prev_hash. | ASM-1168 | The rwb-integration login, the element names of the append command, of the P1 EFS and contact reads and of the five fact answers, the bodies of the two admin operations and the shape of the RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY task are taken as follows. The service runs as the rwb-integration login (DP-02), granted on schema rwb_integration only, its name supplied by the ACE DB story of the service and never written in a story or a value. The append command carries caseId, eventCode, channel, direction, occurredAt, sourceSystem, contactKey, fromHolderRef, toHolderRef, treatmentId, proceedsId, deliveryStatus, externalRef and idempotencyKey. The append answers 201 with an entry reference, 200 with the same reference for a key already held, 409 for a conflicting key, 422 for an invalid command and 503 when the store is unavailable. The admin list answers the delivery id, the event type, the consumer, the status, the attempt count, the next attempt time, the last error code, the delivered time, the task id and the page envelope, and the resend answers the same delivery with status PENDING and attempt count 0. | ASM-1297 | ApprovalRequested and ApprovalDecided carry the approval reference, caseId, decision code, capability area, routed role, routed holder when there is one, approval level, limit version, due time, approval status (WAITING or HELD_NO_LIMIT), preparer user reference, and on a decision the final call with the rule ID and version and the resume state. rwb-case writes one task row with element_type DECISION_TASK, task_code APPROVAL, owner_role from the event, due_at from the event, status OPEN, and the approval reference and preparer reference in the assumed columns of the task shape; on a return it opens one task with element_type HUMAN_TASK and task_code APPROVAL_RETURN for the preparer. | ASM-1298 | While an approval on the case is open the case status is WAITING_APPROVAL, for an approval stored WAITING and for one held as HELD_NO_LIMIT; a held approval opens no decision task because no approver is named and the case still waits. APPROVED, REFUSED and RETURNED each return the case status to IN_PROGRESS; on REFUSED the route_state takes the resume state the routing rule named in the decision (for a settlement below the floor, R-SET-07 and DECLINED_BY_APPROVER_SET), and no case status is added to LOV-CASE-STATUS for either outcome. A case on hold keeps ON_HOLD and writes WAITING_APPROVAL to status_before_hold. | The legacy story says only that the case becomes Waiting approval or returns to the state the rule names, and LOV-CASE-STATUS has no state per approval outcome, so the status that accompanies the rule-named state has to be fixed for the case to be testable. | Legacy RWB-E2-013 sections 9 and 11; TSD P3 v3 T3.2 LOV-CASE-STATUS and T3.1 recovery_case status, route_state and status_before_hold; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-SET-07 and R-UNI-42; FSD P3 v4 A2.3 | GAP-0732 | 4 Flow steps 7, 8, 11 and 13; 7 AC8, AC14; 8 BR14; 9 State transitions; 11 Data | Medium | Business lead and the rwb-case owner at the story review | The status list is unchanged and no new status is added; the refusal keeps the rule-named route state, so the routing behaviour the business agreed is preserved. | B-P3-05 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |

| ASM-1399 | A role conflict refuses the session with MSG-P4-006 naming the pair, and the refusal and the incident it raises are one refusal fact with reason code ROLE_CONFLICT. | The legacy criterion requires an incident on the security administrator queue, and no source of the read set names an incident operation, a queue or a target service, so the refusal fact is the only channel that exists. | RWB-E1-022 section 5 X4 and section 7 AC6; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (P4 publishes no event); RWB-P4-E1039-APP's access-entry writer | GAP-0775 | RWB-P4-E1022-APP sections 4, 5, 9 and 12.8 | Medium | Security administrator role owner and the audit owner at the wave 1 design gate | Gives the incident an addressee through the record that already exists; a dedicated incident operation would be a new contract and is not created | B-P4-01 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1400 | An unmapped or inactive group gives no role, and its name is written on the sign-in fact as a group name only, never as a person's attribute. | The ownership and the FSD agree that a group with no active role row confers nothing, and the legacy criterion also requires the unmapped name to be visible, so the fact must carry a name whose kind has to be fixed to keep personal data out. | RWB-E1-022 section 5 X6, section 8 BR1 and section 7 AC8; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-04; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 35 | GAP-0775 | RWB-P4-E1022-APP sections 4, 5, 8 and 9 | High | rwb-access service owner at the wave 1 design gate | The fact carries a group name and a reference; no person attribute reaches a log or an event | B-P4-01 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1401 | rwb-access caches nothing of another service's data: the reference values and the team and region codes are read per call through the rwb-case contracts, and no row is copied into rwb_access. | The reference lists and the teams are P3's under the ownership map, and a copy in rwb_access would be a second source that drifts at the first version change; the schema story states that no object of rwb_access references rwb_case. | Ownership Map v1 (lov_value, reference_row, reference_version, queue, queue_member owned by P3); DP-01 and DP-07; RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON; RWB-P3-E1019-CON | GAP-0775 | RWB-P4-E1022-APP sections 3, 5, 11, 12.2 and 17 | High | rwb-access service owner and the rwb-case service owner at the wave 1 contract freeze | One hop per resolution for the values and the team codes; no local copy, no local invalidation and no drift | B-P4-01 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1402 | The sign-in and refusal facts are written locally by the access-entry writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP and published to rwb.decision-record.v1; this story supplies the reference, the area, the right, the result and the reason code and builds no writer of its own. | The access log is written locally and published to the decision topic, and the writer is one story of this service; a second writer inside the resolver would duplicate the record path and the hash chain. | Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20 (every service writes its own decision records) and 22; DP-03; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; RWB-E1-022 section 13 build step 5 | GAP-0775 | RWB-P4-E1022-APP sections 4, 5, 12.8 and 13 | High | rwb-access service owner and the audit owner at the wave 1 design gate | One record path for every refusal and sign-in; the resolver adds no writer, no table and no topic | B-P4-01 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1403 | The two operations of the access contract are published at POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions, built from the operation names of Architecture v5 slide 14 and the base rule of section R4. | The slide names the operations and the Ownership Map has no path row for either, so the base rule is the only published derivation of a path; leaving it open would leave every consumer guessing the same two strings. | Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; Template and Rules section R4 and DP-13; Ownership Map v1 api list (no row for authorise or me/permissions) | GAP-0776 | RWB-P4-E1022-CON sections 1, 3, 7 AC1, 12.1 and 13 | High | Contract owner of rwb-access and the platform edge owner at the contract freeze | Fixes two paths and no payload; a later Ownership Map path row would replace the assumption and not the operations | B-P4-01 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1404 | The authorise request carries the role codes of the resolved session, the scope type with the team and region codes, the capability area, the right and the delegation band key of the action, and the answer carries the decision, the matrix version, the conflict version and on a refusal the reason code and the message id. | No source fixes the payload: the legacy contract was a Java method over a SessionContext type and the slide names only the inputs role, scope and DoA, so the contract must state the shape it publishes and say that it is stated. | RWB-E1-022 section 12; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (POST /authorise: role, scope, DoA) and slide 11 (REST, one hop, 2 s); TSD P4 v3 T-A.2 API-P4-012 (the resolved session holds roles, scope, matrix and conflict versions) | GAP-0776 | RWB-P4-E1022-CON sections 4, 7 AC2 and AC3, and 12.1 | Medium | Contract owner of rwb-access with the consuming squads at the contract freeze | Fixes the shape every consumer compiles against; it carries identifiers and version labels only and no business value | B-P4-01 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |

| ASM-1406 | The role-to-group mapping rows stay in role.entra_group as TSD P4 v3 defines them, the ACE group facts behind a mapping are read only through the P1 contract or RWB-P1-E1069-APP, and no object of rwb_access names an ACE schema, the recovery schema or public. | FSD P4 v3 reads the mapping from v_ace_iam_group while TSD P4 v3 defines role.entra_group and the mapping contract keeps the rows in the table; R-PREC puts the technical specification above the functional one, and the boundary rule forbids a service reading ACE directly. | FSD P4 v3 A2.1 field catalog; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 role (DF-REF-039); Template and Rules section R3 R-PREC items 6 and 7; Ownership Map v1 role row; RWB-P1-E1069-APP (the ACE view owner) | GAP-0777 | RWB-P4-E1022-DB sections 1, 3, 7 AC6, 11 and 17 | Medium | P4 service owner, the P1 data owner and the architecture review at the wave 1 schema gate | Keeps one mapping row set in rwb_access and one read path for the ACE facts; no view, synonym or grant crosses the schema boundary | B-P4-01 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |

| ASM-1408 | A matrix version and a masking version resolve at sign-in and stay until the session ends, so open work keeps the version it signed in under and a new version answers only new sessions. | The legacy flow step 5 keeps open sessions on their version and RWB-E1-022 resolves the version at sign-in; no source states the rule for the split service. | Legacy RWB-E1-037 section 4 step 5; FSD P4 A2.4; RWB-P4-E1022-APP | GAP-0778 | RWB-P4-E1037-APP sections 2, 4 and 12.1 | Medium | Solution architect with the access owner | A withdrawn permission stays in force for the life of an open session, up to the session timeout; the alternative is a per-request resolve, which costs one read per call. | B-P4-01 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |

| ASM-1412 | The access log is written locally through the decision-record library to rwb.decision-record.v1 and the central ledger stays with P7; a refused call is passed to the access-entry writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP, which P4 owns and which writes no P7 table. | DP-03 moves the decision log to a local library plus the shared topic, and the access log is a P4 object that must be written without a P7 table write. | Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-03; Ownership Map (decision_log_entry is P7); Architecture v5 slide 14 (access log in rwb_access) | GAP-0778 | RWB-P4-E1037-APP sections 4 and 12.7; RWB-P4-E1037-CON section 12.7 | High | Solution architect | The access query reads the local ledger copy and the central search is P7's operation; a P4 search over a P7 table is not built. | B-P4-01 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1413 | The membership refresh interval is five minutes, read from the parameter rwb.access.membership-refresh-minutes=5, so a leaver's session ends at the first request after the refresh. | The legacy story assumes the interval (DL38) and no source fixes a value; the parameter keeps it changeable without a build. | Legacy RWB-E1-037 section 4 step 11, section 13 and AC8; DL38 | GAP-0778 | RWB-P4-E1037-APP sections 3 and 4; AC8 | Medium | Security administrator | A leaver keeps access for at most five minutes after the group is removed; a shorter value costs more group reads, a longer one widens the window. | B-P4-01 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |

| ASM-1417 | rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1 carries the change kind (matrix or masking), the version label, the effective date and the approver reference, and never a field value, a person, a case id or a letter of a role. | Arch v5 slide 14 names the event and fixes no payload; the data-minimisation rule of NFR-040 and the no-personal-data rule of slide 35 fix what it may not carry. | Architecture v5 slide 14 and slide 35; NFR-040; RWB-PLT-E1037-CON AC3 and AC5 | GAP-0779 | RWB-P4-E1037-CON sections 2, 8 (BR8) and 12.3; RWB-P4-E1037-APP section 12.3 | Medium | Solution architect with the event platform owner | A consumer that needs more than the version label must call the matrix read; a richer payload would carry policy data over the topic. | B-P4-01 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1418 | The rwb_access baseline objects role, permission, masking_rule, role_conflict and delegation_limit are created by the service template migration V0001 of RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, and this legacy key adds only its two unique indexes, because WP B-P4-01 carries no DB story for RWB-E1-037. | The service template owns the schema baseline and every service has its own DB story; this key has none in the WP, so the baseline cannot be left unowned. | Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-15 and §R5.7; TSD P4 v3 T3.1; WP B-P4-01 write list (no DB story for RWB-E1-037) | GAP-0778 | RWB-P4-E1037-APP sections 3 and 13; RWB-P4-E1037-CON sections 3 and 12.7 | Medium | ACE DB team with the service owner | If the baseline does not carry the five tables, the index migration fails and a DB story of this key must be created before the first load. | B-P4-01 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1419 | GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles is one path with one contract; RWB-P4-E1019-APP answers the role code, class, default scope and conflict fields and RWB-P4-E1037-APP answers the permission rows and the matrix version of the same answer. | The Ownership Map gives P4 one path and the TSD gives it one purpose (list roles with permissions and scope), so two slices contribute fields to one operation instead of publishing two paths. | Ownership Map (GET /admin/roles is P4); TSD P4 v3 API-P4-007; API Specification v4 /admin/roles x-module P4; RWB-P4-E1019-APP | GAP-0779 | RWB-P4-E1037-CON sections 12.1 and 18; RWB-P4-E1037-APP section 12.1 | Medium | Solution architect with both app owners | Two answers on one path would break the generated client; the merge is at the assembler and one slice must not redefine the other's fields. | B-P4-01 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |

| ASM-1490 | A pair that forbids one role with any business role is carried as one role_conflict row per business role at the same conflict version, because conflicts_with holds one role code of varchar(30) and the schema has no wildcard and no second code list. | The FSD example states that RW-SECADM may not hold any business role, and TSD P4 v3 defines the pair as two single role codes, so the rule the specification describes cannot be stored as one row and its storage has to be decided. | FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (DF-REF-206 LOV-ROLE varchar(20), DF-REF-207 conflicts_with varchar(30)); TSD P4 v3 T6.1 (the business roles of the matrix); RWB-P4-E1019-APP (the role matrix file and its conflict pairs) | GAP-0795 | RWB-P4-AD005-APP sections 1, 3, 8 (BR8), 11 and 13; RWB-P4-AD005-CON sections 7 (AC2) and 8 (BR6) |  |  | The rule is storable without a schema change and the pair count grows with the business roles; a wildcard, if the business wants one, is a column change and a new version of the table | B-P4-02 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1491 | The open incident a grant is bound to is read through an IncidentStatusPort whose adapter is a Day-1 stub: the incident register's owner, store, contract and the incident reference pattern are fixed by no source of this read set, so the port is declared and stubbed rather than tied to a named system. | Legacy AC1 needs an open incident and AC2 a refusal when there is none, while FSD P4 v3 A2.28 names Log Analytics and the Workbench as the path and no incident store, and Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access no incident path and no event. | Legacy RWB-AD-006 AC1 and AC2 and section 5; FSD P4 v3 A2.28, AC-ALT-P4-009-01 and AC-EXC-P4-007-01; Architecture v5 slides 14 and 20; ownership map (no incident api row). | GAP-0797 | RWB-P4-AD006-APP sections 1, 3, 4, 5, 12.2, 12.8, 13; RWB-P4-AD006-CON sections 3, 7, 12.2, 12.8 | Medium | The security administrator and the platform on-call owner | The grant is incident-bound from Day 1 and the check is a port, so the register can be named later with an adapter and no change to the rule, the criteria or the table. | B-P4-02 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1492 | The window in force is 4 hours from the activation, held as the parameter rwb.access.breakglass.window-hours and never as a constant; the code is this key's own and the value 4 hours is the value of the criteria and the tests. | Legacy AC1 says the system grants access for the window and fixes no length, FSD P4 v3 AC-ALT-P4-009-01 shows the activation at 10:30 and the grant active until 14:30, and no source names the parameter that carries the hours. | Legacy RWB-AD-006 AC1 and AC3; FSD P4 v3 AC-ALT-P4-009-01; TSD P4 v3 API-P4-013; DP-06; Template and Rules R5.5. | GAP-0797 | RWB-P4-AD006-APP sections 1, 3, 4, 7, 8, 13; RWB-P4-AD006-CON sections 3, 7, 8, 11 | Medium | The security administrator and the platform parameter owner | A different window is a parameter row and no build; the four hours of the criteria stay the tested value. | B-P4-02 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1493 | The grant is held in break_glass_grant in rwb_access, named and shaped by this key as its own working decision: grant_id, actor_user_id, incident_reference, approval_reference, capability_area, right, scope, reason, starts_at, ends_at, state, ended_at, marker and the entry reference, with no BR Field ID and no ownership-map row. | No grant table exists in TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and the ownership map has no row for one, while the criteria need a stored grant that the guard, the session read and the end operation read. | TSD P4 v3 T3.0 and T3.1; ownership map tables list; legacy RWB-AD-006 section 11; Architecture v5 slides 20 and 41. | GAP-0799 | RWB-P4-AD006-APP sections 1, 3, 11, 12.7, 13; RWB-P4-AD006-CON sections 3, 11, 12.7; RWB-P4-AD006-DB sections 1, 2, 7, 8, 11, 12.7 | Medium | The ACE database engineer and the data steward | One table in the service's own schema, no cross-schema key, and a later official data-model entry is an additive change to the same table. | B-P4-02 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1494 | The end and read operations are this revision's decision at POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants/{grantId}/end with right C and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants/{grantId} with right R, idempotent by Idempotency-Key on the end, because no ownership-map row and no TSD row exists for either. | API-P4-013 publishes only the activation, the legacy Endpoints table gives only the access-log read that is not this story's, and Template and Rules R4 and DP-13 fix the base and the naming rule but not the paths. | TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-P4-013 only); ownership map api list; legacy RWB-AD-006 Endpoints and Permission checks; Template and Rules R4 and DP-13. | GAP-0798 | RWB-P4-AD006-APP sections 1, 12.1; RWB-P4-AD006-CON sections 3, 7, 11, 12.1, 13 | Medium | The solution architect and the security administrator | The lifecycle is complete on Day 1 with three operations on one base, and a later TSD row can adopt the same paths without a consumer change. | B-P4-02 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1495 | No rwb.access event is published for a grant: the grant is session state and not a policy change, its readers are the authorisation guard, the breakGlass field of GET /me/session (API-P4-012) and the access-log marker of RWB-P4-E1039-APP, and the only message it produces is the library's decision-record entry. | Architecture v5 slides 14 and 43 give rwb-access exactly two business events, AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged, both for a cache refresh, and a grant that changes no permission row, no scope and no delegation limit would only cache an entitlement that has already expired. | Architecture v5 slides 11, 14, 20 and 43; TSD P4 v3 T5.3 (events: none); TSD P4 v3 API-P4-012 (session carries the break-glass state); DP-03 and DP-14. | GAP-0798 | RWB-P4-AD006-APP sections 2, 4, 8, 12.3, 12.5; RWB-P4-AD006-CON sections 2, 7, 8, 11, 12.3 | High | The solution architect and the event platform owner | One distributed state only, read on the call; no consumer subscribes to a name that does not exist and no cache holds an expired entitlement. | B-P4-02 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1496 | The clock is the authority over a grant: a grant is in force only while its state is ACTIVE and the time is before ends_at, the guard refuses every call after the window with no job and no person acting, and the row settles to ENDED with its AC-BGOFF entry on the next read, session read or authorised call; a grant nobody touches stays ACTIVE in its row and is out of force by time. | Legacy AC3 requires the grant to end with no action by anyone, and no source gives the service an expiry job or a Schedule: Architecture v5 slide 44 gives rwb-access only the six-monthly access review, so the window must be resolved on the read. | Legacy RWB-AD-006 AC3; Architecture v5 slides 14 and 44; TSD P4 v3 T4; DP-17 (no scheduler in the service beyond the Schedule map). | GAP-0799 | RWB-P4-AD006-APP sections 4, 8, 9, 12.5, 12.6, 13; RWB-P4-AD006-CON sections 7, 8, 9, 12.5, 12.6; RWB-P4-AD006-DB sections 7, 8 | High | The security administrator and the tech lead of rwb-access | No expiry job to lose and no job latency in the refusal; the cost is one UPDATE on the next read, and an untouched row still cannot be used as an entitlement. | B-P4-02 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1497 | The reason is at least 20 characters, the legacy floor, and at most 1000 characters, fixed by the column width and FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-007-02; the floor travels as a parameter (rwb.access.breakglass.reason-min) and is enforced both by the operation and by a check constraint. | Legacy AC1 fixes the minimum of 20 characters and says nothing of a maximum, FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-007-02 fixes the bounds as a validation rule, and no source names the parameter that carries the floor. | Legacy RWB-AD-006 AC1; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-007-02; TSD P4 v3 T3.1; DP-06. | GAP-0797 | RWB-P4-AD006-APP sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 11, 14; RWB-P4-AD006-CON sections 3, 7, 8, 11; RWB-P4-AD006-DB sections 7, 8, 11 | Medium | The security administrator and the compliance officer | A short reason is refused at the door and at the database, and a change of the floor is a parameter row and no build. | B-P4-02 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1498 | The retention of a grant is data: the retention class and the period are parameter rows of the parameters catalogue and never a literal in a migration, the table is not partitioned by this story, and the rollback of the migration drops the table, its constraints and its indexes only. | TSD P4 v3 T-B records DL26 as open for the retention periods, no source fixes a period for a grant, and a partition key would have to be chosen before the period is known. | TSD P4 v3 T-B (DL26 open); Architecture v5 slides 20 and 29; DP-15; DP-06. | GAP-0799 | RWB-P4-AD006-DB sections 1, 3, 7, 8, 11, 12.7, 13 | Medium | The ACE database engineer and the compliance officer | A period set at DL26 is a row, not a migration; the table carries no partition key it would later have to lose, and the rollback leaves the schema as the baseline found it. | B-P4-02 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1499 | The security administrator's approval is an IAM request outside the Workbench: the grant holds its reference as approval_reference and the approver reference beside it, the caller cannot approve the request it activates, and the Workbench runs no approval workflow of its own for a grant. | TSD P4 v3 API-P4-013 says the grant is approved in the bank IAM and activates it in the Workbench, FSD P4 v3 AC-ALT-P4-009-01 and AC-EXC-P4-007-01 put the approval and the emergency group in the bank IAM, and Architecture v5 gives rwb-access no approval workflow. | TSD P4 v3 API-P4-013 and T6.1; FSD P4 v3 AC-ALT-P4-009-01 and AC-EXC-P4-007-01; Architecture v5 slide 14 (ApprovalWorkflow belongs to rwb-decision); legacy RWB-AD-006 AC1. | GAP-0797 | RWB-P4-AD006-APP sections 3, 4, 8, 10, 12.5; RWB-P4-AD006-CON sections 3, 8, 11, 12.5 | Medium | The security administrator and the bank IAM owner | No second approval workflow is built, the four-eyes control stays where the bank already runs it, and the Workbench can always show who approved and when. | B-P4-02 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1500 | A person holds at most one active grant: the state values are ACTIVE, ENDED and REFUSED, and a unique partial index on actor_user_id where state = ACTIVE makes the database refuse a second active row for the same actor. | FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-007-05 fixes the one-active-grant rule, the legacy story fixes no state vocabulary, and TSD P4 v3 T3.1 defines no grant table, so the states and the enforcement are this key's own. | FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-007-05; legacy RWB-AD-006 AC1; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and T3.2; DP-15. | GAP-0799 | RWB-P4-AD006-APP sections 4, 5, 8, 9, 11; RWB-P4-AD006-CON sections 7, 8, 9, 11; RWB-P4-AD006-DB sections 7, 8, 11, 12.7 | Medium | The security administrator and the ACE database engineer | Two emergency windows cannot overlap for one person even under a race, and the state field has one vocabulary across the app, the contract and the schema. | B-P4-02 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |

| ASM-1502 | The access-log search answers from the entries the local decision-record chain of rwb_access holds (AC-READ, AC-DENY, AC-EXPT) and every answer names the chain and the period it covers; the end-to-end view over the central ledger is the integration story's. | The entry is written by its owner in the owner's schema and collected centrally within five minutes, so the local chain is the first complete answer for the events this service produced, and the sources name no cross-ledger query. | Architecture v5 slide 28 and slide 41; TSD P4 v3 API-P4-008; DP-01 and DP-03. | GAP-0801 | RWB-P4-AD007-APP sections 1, 4, 8, 11, 12.7, 19; RWB-P4-AD007-CON sections 10, 11, 12.7 | Medium | Internal audit and the tech lead of rwb-decision | The search covers one service's chain; a cross-estate query needs the P7 query API and the integration harness. | B-P4-03 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1503 | The export is text/csv in UTF-8 with one header row and the columns decided_at, decision_code, actor_reference, capability_area, right, case_reference, document_reference, data_product_reference, role_code, matrix_version, masking_version, grant_id, incident_reference; the screen shows the same columns in the same order, the cap is 10,000 rows and the answer above it is 422. | Legacy AC2 fixes only that the file carries the same masking as the screen, and the audit consumer needs one fixed column order to attach the file as evidence. | RWB-AD-007 AC2 and TC-AD-007-02; FSD P4 v3 A2.7 and A2.16; TSD P4 v3 API-P4-008. | GAP-0802 | RWB-P4-AD007-APP sections 4, 8, 12.1, 14; RWB-P4-AD007-CON sections 7, 11, 12.1 | Medium | Internal audit and the integration and QA team | A column change is a contract change within major version 1 and is reviewed as an additive change only. | B-P4-03 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1504 | The masking version recorded on an entry is the version that masks it in the answer and in the export, and it is shown in the masking_version column; a later masking version does not rewrite an old entry. | The entry records the version it was written under, so re-masking under a current rule would make the file disagree with the entry it evidences. | TSD P4 v3 T3.1 masking_rule DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204; FSD P4 v3 A2.7; NFR-039. | GAP-0803 | RWB-P4-AD007-APP sections 8, 11, 15; RWB-P4-AD007-CON section 15 | Medium | Compliance and PDPA officer and the data steward | An old export stays masked as it was at the time of the access, and the version is auditable from the file itself. | B-P4-03 | Unconfirmed (business decision pending) |

| ASM-1509 | The removal of an unconfirmed holder is requested through the ACE Common group membership path of INT-21; the request carries the group of the role, the role code, the holder user reference and the review, the answer carries a request reference and whether it was accepted, and on failure the item stays open with a follow-up task and an incident until it is answered. | Legacy AC2 requires the removal request and no source gives the bank IAM removal a contract, so the path and its failure handling have to be fixed before the close can be built. | TSD P4 v3 T5.1 INT-21; TSD P2 v3 INT-21; Arch v5 slides 14 and 41; Legacy RWB-AD-008 AC2 | GAP-0808 | RWB-P4-AD008-APP section 4 Flow steps 16 and 17; section 5 Exception paths X11; section 7 AC2 and AC5; section 12.2 and 12.8 Contract; section 13 Build step 7 | Medium | ACE team integration owner and the solution architect before the wave 4 harness is written | A different removal contract changes the client, the fake and the failure path only; the item states, the entry and the messages stay as specified. | B-P4-03 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1510 | The owner of a role is the holder of the A letter in Platform administration for that role, which TSD P4 T6.1 gives to RW-SECADM (CRUDA) and RW-PLATADM (CRUD), and RW-COE owns the reference-data roles; a caller with R only owns no role, sees no holder and is refused with MSG-P4-002. | The legacy story gives the list to each role owner, the permission check gives six roles Platform administration R, and no source says which of them may certify, so the ownership test would otherwise be invented per screen. | Legacy RWB-AD-008 Story line and Permission checks; TSD P4 v3 T6.1; FSD P4 v3 A2.13 and A2.30 | GAP-0809 | RWB-P4-AD008-APP section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow step 8; section 7 AC3 and AC4; section 8 BR4; section 10 Authority; section 12.1 Contract | Medium | Security administrator and the solution architect at the access model review | A different ownership rule changes the scoping read and the 403 cases; the operations, the entry and the four-eyes rule stay as specified. | B-P4-03 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1511 | A holder with no decision at the close is not confirmed, and its removal is requested at the close through the ACE Common path within the DL38 leaver interval of the same working day. | Legacy AC2 acts on a holder not confirmed by the end of the review and no source defines the state, so the close would otherwise have no trigger. | Legacy RWB-AD-008 AC2; DL38; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 JOB-18 | GAP-0810 | RWB-P4-AD008-APP section 4 Flow step 16; section 7 AC2 and AC5; section 8 BR8; section 9 State transitions; section 12.6 Schedules | Medium | Security administrator at the access model review | Documentation and one close rule; a different definition changes only the close step and its test case. | B-P4-03 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1512 | rwb-access provides the console ingest of a list of values and its checks under /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/lov-loads, and rwb-case stores and versions the rows through its own reference-load contract; the two paths and the request field name are reconciled at contract review before the endpoint is frozen. | The TSD P4 v3 puts the paths and lov_value in the access module while the R-PREC default ruling puts reference data with P3, and no source names the public console path. | Ownership Map v1 rulings ASM-A6-tables-5 and ASM-A6-api-4; TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 and T3.1; Template and Rules v1 R3 | GAP-0811 | APP s1, s3, s4, s10, s12.1, s12.2, s12.7; CON s3, s7 AC1 and AC5, s11, s12.1, s12.7 | Medium | Solution architect, with the rwb-case and rwb-access tech leads at contract review | If the review moves the ingest to rwb-case, the app story keeps the checks and loses the two provided operations, and the CON baseline is reissued | B-P4-03 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |

| ASM-1545 | The rule arm of the gate is built against the P7 rule-package rollback contract and its fake: POST /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/rollback takes the reason and answers the restored version, its state and its effective-from time, and the missing C dependency RWB-P7-AD013-CON (or the id the P7 split allocates) is added to the metadata at D1. | The rule half is P7's under the R-PREC default ruling and the ownership map, while the story's contract-dependency list names two P3 contracts and no P7 contract; the gate cannot be built without a fixed operation, so a default is taken on Day 1. | Ownership map (rule_package_version ruling ASM-A6-tables-3; api ruling ASM-A6-api-3); TSD P4 v3 API-P4-018; Temporal and Drools slide 15 notes; WP B-P4-04 metadata for RWB-P4-AD013-APP | GAP-0844 | Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 12.2 Contract; section 12.8 Contract fakes; section 13 Build step 6 | Medium | Solution architect and the P7 rwb-decision tech lead when the P7 rule-package contract is published | If the P7 operation renames a field or a path, only OwnerRollbackClient, its fake and the contract test change; the gate, the record and the two entries stay as specified. | B-P4-04 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1546 | The gate provides POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/version-rollbacks and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/version-rollbacks/{rollbackId}; the read is served from the stored answer of the accepted call in the platform idempotency table and its two decision-record entries, not from either owner. | No source declares an rwb-access rollback path and no source declares a rollback resource that survives the request; the read must come from somewhere the record already owns, and asking an owner again would let the read disagree with the record. | API Specification v4 index; TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 and T-A.2; legacy RWB-AD-013 endpoints; DP-09 and DP-13 | GAP-0845 | Section 1 Story; section 12.1 Contract; section 12.9 Call-type summary; section 13 Components | Medium | Solution architect, the console lead and both owner tech leads at contract review | A different path changes the two operations, the fakes and the composite route only; the gate's rules are unaffected. | B-P4-04 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |

| ASM-1571 | The rule-change request is a record of rwb-access and not a table of rwb-access: one entry of the local decision-record chain of the DP-03 library, written with an idempotency row in the same transaction, with the rule package version consumed through the P7 contract and its fake. The missing RWB-P7 rule-package contract dependency is raised at D1 and is not added to the metadata of this story. | The rule registry, its versions and its rows are P7's under ASM-A6-tables-3 and ASM-A6-api-3, so this service can neither hold the version nor read a rule table, while an administrative decision that is not recorded cannot be defended; the sources name no table and no operation for the change request itself. | TSD P4 v3 T6.3 and T4; Temporal and Drools design slide 15 (governance central in rwb-decision); ownership map rows rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case and the rule-package API paths (ASM-A6-tables-3, ASM-A6-api-3); DP-01 and DP-03. | GAP-0868 | RWB-P4-E8007-APP sections 1, 4, 11, 12.1, 12.2, 12.7, 12.8, 19; RWB-P4-E8007-CON sections 11, 12.2, 12.7, 12.8 | Medium | Tech lead of rwb-decision and the tech lead of rwb-access | A cross-service change record needs a registry table or a central record instead of the local chain, and the audit consumer would read P7 rather than rwb-access. | B-P4-05 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1572 | The seven items of TSD P4 v3 T6.3 — request, impact, test result, approver, load, verify and rollback plan — are the change checklist of the change request, checked for completeness when the change is raised and carried as the seven required item codes of the RuleChangeChecklist schema; a missing item is refused 422 with MSG-P3-022 naming the item code. | The technical specification attaches the checklist to the approval of a version and names no check at the point where the change is raised, and this story must refuse an incomplete change before any registry hop so the analyst learns the missing item while the change is still only a form. | TSD P4 v3 T6.3 (change_checklist, DF-REF-295, MSG-P3-022); FSD P4 v3 A2.18; the message table of the rule-change stories for the text of MSG-P3-022; the pattern list of the key holds no DP07 and the contract-dependency list no RWB-P3-E1043-CON, so the item codes are contract constants rather than a reference-data read. | GAP-0868 | RWB-P4-E8007-APP sections 3, 4, 8, 12.1, 12.8; RWB-P4-E8007-CON sections 7 (AC2), 8, 11, 12.1, 14 | Medium | Centre of excellence and the internal audit representative | If the checklist belongs only to the approval, the change request carries the items as reference and the registry remains the only gate; the 422 of an incomplete change would then become a warning and no change would be refused here. | B-P4-05 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1573 | The record code of an administrative change is the administrative-change code of the local decision-record library, and the change entry is written under it with the change id in the reference field of the entry; the change id is minted by this service and is opaque to every consumer. | The sources fix the decision codes of a case decision and of an access event and give no code for an administrative change, and the entry must be findable by the identifier the screen and the audit quote. | TSD P4 v3 T6.3 (a change log entry is append only, with the version label, the status change, the author or approver and the time); LDM v8 DF-DEC-003 for the decision code and DF-DEC-008 for the reference field; DP-03 for the local library. | GAP-0868 | RWB-P4-E8007-APP sections 4, 8, 11, 12.3, 12.7; RWB-P4-E8007-CON sections 8 (BR11), 11, 12.3, 12.7 | Medium | Tech lead of rwb-access and the owner of the decision-record library | A different record code changes the value written on every change entry and the filter the audit consumer uses; the entry would still be found by its change id. | B-P4-05 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1574 | A move writes a new delegation_limit row that carries the next limit_version of the same limit in state PENDING_APPROVAL, and the row in force is changed only at the approval, when it is closed with valid_to and state SUPERSEDED; the decision code, the level, the product group and the conditions of the moved row are copied from the row it moves, because this story's pattern list carries no DP-07 and its contract-dependency list no RWB-P3-E1043-CON. | The legacy story and the FSD name the move and no row model, and the table is a version-carrying table of this service, so the change has to be modelled either as an edit of the row in force or as a new row version; an edit would let a limit change before Risk approves it. | FSD P4 v3 A2.19 and A2.6.4.2; TSD P4 v3 T3.0 (state, version), T3.1 delegation_limit DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026 and DF-REF-055 to DF-REF-062; Temporal and Drools design (versioned limits, approve-and-date); Architecture v5 slide 14; ownership map ASM-A6-tables-4. | GAP-0869 | RWB-P4-E8008-APP sections 1, 3, 4, 8, 9, 11, 12.7; RWB-P4-E8008-CON sections 7 (AC2, AC3), 8, 9, 11 | Medium | Risk and model risk officer and the tech lead of RWB-P4-E1038-APP | If a move must edit the row in force instead, the approval gate disappears and the lookup of RWB-P4-E2013-APP can answer a limit that Risk has not approved. | B-P4-05 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1575 | The row a move supersedes carries valid_to as the day before the valid_from of the row that supersedes it, and its state becomes SUPERSEDED in the same transaction as the approval, so exactly one version of a limit is in force on any date. | The sources fix that rows stay readable with a valid_to once a new version is approved and name no rule for the closing date of a move, so the day-before rule has to be chosen or two rows would be in force on the effective date. | FSD P4 v3 A2.6.4.2 (the rows of DOA-2026.11 stay readable with valid_to 2026-12-31 while DOA-2027.01 is in force from 2027-01-01); TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-025 and DF-REF-026; Temporal and Drools design. | GAP-0869 | RWB-P4-E8008-APP sections 4, 8, 9, 12.1; RWB-P4-E8008-CON sections 7 (AC3), 8, 9 | Medium | Risk and model risk officer and the tech lead of rwb-access | A different closing date leaves two rows in force on the day a change takes effect, and the lookup of RWB-P4-E2013-APP would answer the lower level or the higher one depending on the order of the rows. | B-P4-05 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1576 | The change event rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1 is published on rwb.access.events.v1, keyed by delegationLimitId, with the payload delegationLimitId, limitVersion, decisionCode, approvalLevel, productGroup, effectiveFrom and reason, and with no holder reference, no substitute reference and no personal data. | Architecture v5 names the event on the topic and names no payload, so the field list and the exclusion of the person references have to be fixed or the event would either be unusable by a subscriber or publish the delegation table's person references to every consumer. | Architecture v5 slide 14 and slide 41 (rwb.access.events.v1: AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged); TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-017 to DF-REF-019, DF-REF-023, DF-REF-024 and DF-REF-055; NFR-040; DP-09. | GAP-0869 | RWB-P4-E8008-APP sections 1, 4, 8, 12.3, 17; RWB-P4-E8008-CON sections 7 (AC3, AC6), 11, 12.3, 17 | Medium | Risk and model risk officer and the data steward | A payload that carries the holder or the substitute publishes person references to every subscriber; a payload without the version or the effective date cannot be used to refresh a limit cache. | B-P4-05 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1577 | The treatment policy edition travels as one workbook file that rwb-access passes unchanged to P3 rwb-case POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads with the table code product_policy and the valid-from date, so every band, floor and range stays with its owner and this service reads out of the file only the presence of its three parts and their row counts. The three parts are one sheet each for the bands, the floors and the ranges, each with a header row; the sheet names, the header rows, the accepted media types and the upload size cap are fixed at contract review with the owner. The state of a load is read through the owner's load read GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}, declared as consumed although the TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A does not list it, and the screen that carries the edition is served through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 because no source names it. The reference-load contract is called through its contract and its fake and is not added to the metadata dependency rows. | The parameters and reference data, the reference-load operations and the treatment entity belong to other services under the R-PREC default ruling and the ownership map, and no source gives the table code, the sheet names or a load read, so the transport and the parts have to be fixed as a default before the build; leaving them open would stop the story and inviting the values into rwb-access would create a second copy of a versioned table. | Template and Rules v1 section R3 default ruling and R5.5 DP-07; TSD P4 v3 T3.2, T4 and appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-P4-004 to API-P4-010); FSD P4 v3 A2.20.2; Program BRD REQ-DRI-010; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (lov_value, reference_version, reference_row, treatment, POST /admin/reference-loads); legacy RWB-E8-009 story statement | GAP-0870 | Section 1; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 5, 8 and 12; section 5 X3 and X8; section 7 AC4; section 8 BR1, BR3, BR6 and BR10; section 11 Data; section 12.1, 12.2, 12.7 and 12.8; section 13; section 15 | Medium | Solution architect and the tech lead of rwb-case (P3) at the contract review of RWB-P4-E8009-CON, with the product head as the business reader | A renamed table code, a different set of sheet names or an owner-side load read of another shape changes the controller, the client and the fake only, with no change to the rights, the messages or the record content; if the owner refuses to accept a pass-through file, the edition would have to be modelled as a value set and the ownership ruling would have to change first. | B-P4-05 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1578 | The product head proposes the edition and does not submit it. TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives RW-PRODHEAD R only in Rules and parameters, RW-COE CRUD there and RW-RISK RA there, and the legacy permission table gives the C letter to RW-COE and the A letter to RW-RISK. R-PREC puts the Technical Specifications above the story master, and the FSD makes the product head the primary role of the feature, so the story reads the three sources together as: the product head opens the screen, prepares the edition and proposes it with R; a holder of the C letter, RW-COE, submits it through POST /admin/product-policies; and the A letter approves a load on the console reference-load path, which is RWB-P4-AD010-APP's and not this story's. A product head posting an edition is therefore refused 403 with MSG-P4-002, which is the refusal AC3 tests. | Three sources disagree on who may act: the FSD calls the product head primary, the TSD gives it R only, and the legacy table gives the C letter to RW-COE; a story that silently granted the product head the C letter would contradict the matrix and a story that removed the product head from the feature would contradict the FSD, so the reading has to be recorded before the build. | FSD P4 v3 A2.20.3.3 and A2.20.4.1; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and the rule package and workflow refinement table; legacy RWB-E8-009 permission checks; Template and Rules v1 section R3 R-PREC order and §R5.5 DP-08 (the matrix is data); Program BRD REQ-ACA-003 and REQ-ACA-013 | GAP-0870 | Section 2; section 5 X5 and X11; section 7 AC3; section 8 BR4 and BR5; section 10 Authority; section 12.1; section 14; and in the contract story section 7 AC1, section 8 BR7, section 10 and section 12.1 | Medium | Solution architect with the owner of the permission matrix and the product head as the business reader, at the contract review of RWB-P4-E8009-CON; a change is a permission row and not a code change | If the matrix is later changed to give RW-PRODHEAD the C letter, AC3 changes to the opposite answer and only a permission row and that one test change; if the four-eyes reading is rejected, RW-COE submits and RW-RISK approves the load and this story's own operations are unaffected. | B-P4-05 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1579 | An accepted edition appends exactly one entry to the local decision-record chain of DP-03 carrying the editionId, the productGroup, the policyVersion label, the loadId the owner answered, the validFrom date, the version in force read from the parameters contract at the time and the caller reference, and nothing else: no band, no floor, no range, no amount, no percentage and no personal field. The record code that marks the entry as a treatment policy edition is not in any source, so the entry uses the DP-03 library's administrative-change code and the contract review fixes the value with the ledger owner. The entry, the idempotency row and the answer commit in one local transaction, and where the entry cannot be written the answer is withheld with 503 and MSG-P7-003, which is what legacy AC2 asserts as nothing changing. | Legacy AC1 requires the result to be written to the decision log with the rule version, and legacy AC2 requires nothing to change when the log cannot be written, but no source names the record code of an administrative change or says which version label the entry carries; the record has to be fixed as a default or neither criterion can be tested. | Legacy RWB-E8-009 AC1 and AC2, the message table and the data table (DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018); TSD P4 v3 T3.2, T4 and T6.3 (the change log entry of a load, an approval and a rollback is append only); FSD P4 v3 A2.20.4.1 and A2.20.4.3 (AC-EXC-P4-020-02); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-03; Program BRD REQ-DRI-010 | GAP-0870 | Section 4 Flow steps 10 and 11; section 5 X9; section 7 AC2 and AC5; section 8 BR8 and BR9; section 11 Data; section 12.3 and 12.7; section 13 Database and migrations; and in the contract story section 11, section 12.3 and section 14 | Medium | Tech lead of rwb-access with the ledger owner of rwb-decision (P7) at the contract review of RWB-P4-E8009-CON | A different record code or a different set of carried fields changes the entry writer, the contract's record declaration and one test; the transaction rule and the MSG-P7-003 refusal do not change. | B-P4-05 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1580 | The letter template version lives in rwb-comms and this story is the approval gate and the record: rwb-access reads the version through the P6 contract, hands the approval to the P6 approve operation, records the approving role code and the time in its own decision-record chain and answers the history from that chain; it reads no template, notice or merge-field row and holds no copy of a template body, a merge field or a template state. | The legacy story holds the template and the notice in one schema with the decision log, and the ownership map moves all three template tables to P6 while the metadata of this story carries no P6 contract dependency; the split between the gate and the owner of the template has to be fixed on Day 1, or the story would either invent a dependency it may not add or read a foreign table it may not read. | Ownership Map v1 (template, notice, merge_field = P6; API POST /admin/templates and POST /admin/templates/{templateId}/approve = P6); Architecture v5 slide 41; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 and appendix T-A API-P6-003 to API-P6-007; TSD P4 v3 T6.3; FSD P4 v3 A2.21; Template and Rules R5.4 dependency class C and R5.5 DP-01 | GAP-0871 | Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 6 to 16; section 8 Business rule BR5; section 11 Data; section 12.2 and 12.7 Contract; section 13 Build step 3 | Medium | Solution architect and the P6 rwb-comms tech lead when the P6 template contract is published | If the P6 contract renames a path or a field, or answers the read by id differently, only CommsTemplateClient, its fake and the contract test change; the gate, its two refusals and the history stay as specified. The missing C dependency is added to the metadata at D1 and no template table enters rwb_access. | B-P4-05 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1581 | The approving role recorded on a template approval is RW-COMPLY, the role the FSD A2.21.3.3 role table names, while the right that opens the gate is Rules and parameters A of TSD P4 v3 T6.1, which that matrix gives to RW-RISK (RA) and RW-COE (CRUD) and not to RW-COMPLY (R only); the SIT approver holds RW-COMPLY and holds the A letter, and the four-eyes rule of T6.3 holds in either reading, because the author of a version can never approve it. | The FSD role table and the T6.1 matrix disagree on who approves a letter template, R-PREC puts the technical specification above the functional one, and a story may not change a metadata value; without a default the recorded role code, the right that is authorised and the test data would contradict one another. | FSD P4 v3 A2.21.3.3 roles and permissions; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 RBAC matrix; TSD P4 v3 T6.3 author and approver; legacy RWB-E8-010 permission checks (Rules and parameters C for RW-COE and A for RW-RISK); Template and Rules R3 R-PREC | GAP-0871 | Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 5 and 8; section 7 Background and AC4; section 8 Business rules BR3, BR4 and BR6; section 10 Authority; section 13 Configuration and reference data | Medium | Solution architect with Compliance and the access administrator at the P4 design review | If the matrix is corrected to give RW-COMPLY the A letter, or if Compliance is read to approve under the RW-RISK letter, only the role-to-letters row and the SIT test users change; the gate, the four-eyes refusal and the field that records the approving role code do not. | B-P4-05 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1582 | The approval history answers, for each approved version, the template version, the state APPROVED, the approving role code, the time of the approval and the approval reference, and never a name, an e-mail address or a user reference: the approver user reference that rwb-comms holds in approved_by stays with rwb-comms and is not answered by this service. | REQ-OCC-002 asks that the approval be recorded against the version and the template table holds the approver as a user reference (DF-REF-063), while the record of a decision may not copy personal data into its payload or its reads; a default is needed on what the history says about who approved a version. | TSD P6 v2 T3.1 DF-REF-063 approved_by, DF-REF-064 approved_at and DF-REF-065 valid_from; TSD P4 v3 T6.3 author and approver; REQ-OCC-002; NFR-040; the guardrails of the legacy story RWB-E8-010 | GAP-0871 | Section 1 Story; section 7 AC5; section 8 Business rules BR6, BR8, BR9 and BR10; section 11 Data; section 12.1 Contract; section 17 Guardrails | High | Data steward with Internal audit at the contract review | If audit needs the person, the answer is a second read of the rwb-comms approval and not a field of this service's record; the history fields, the entry payload and the tests do not change. | B-P4-05 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1583 | A configuration version of the access panel of P4 is the triple of permission.matrix_version, masking_rule.masking_version and delegation_limit.limit_version over rows this service owns, with the valid_from and valid_to those rows carry, and no new table; the partner panel, the partner firm, the partner users and the fee schedule stay with S9 rwb-partner and FEAT-PRM-02 is not a prerequisite of this key; the effective-date bounds and the page bounds are parameter rows of rwb-case read through DP-06 with the version in force. | No source defines a configuration-version object, declares a publication operation, gives the matrix label a date column, or gives a value for the bounds, and the legacy key's panel name collides with the partner panel of S9. | Read the version as a label triple over permission, masking_rule and delegation_limit; read the two derived states from the rows' dates and the other five from the decision-record entry; read the bounds and the page limits through the parameters contract and hold no bound in code; read the partner panel as S9's and call it not at all. | GAP-0872 | RWB-P4-E8012-CON sections 1, 3, 8, 11, 12.1, 12.7; RWB-P4-E8012-APP sections 1, 3, 8, 11 | Medium | Solution architect with the rwb-access tech lead and the rwb-case tech lead before the two operations are frozen | Fixes the two paths, the version identity, the state derivations and the bound names; changes no metadata value and adds no dependency | B-P4-06 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1584 | The effective date of a configuration version is resolved at read time by the own authorise operation as the version whose valid_from is on or before today and whose valid_to is after today, so the publication adds no Temporal Schedule, no workflow and no promotion job. | TSD P4 v3 T4 describes the lifecycle of a rule package version and no promotion job for an access-panel version, and Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access one Schedule only, the six-monthly access review list. | Read the version in force from the rows' dates at each authorise call and cache the answer; declare no Schedule and no workflow in the contract and add none to the rwb-access queue. | GAP-0872 | RWB-P4-E8012-CON sections 1, 8, 9, 12.5, 12.6, 17; RWB-P4-E8012-APP sections 1, 8, 9, 12.6, 17 | Medium | Solution architect and the Temporal platform owner at the contract review | Keeps one Schedule on the rwb-access queue and makes the effective date data rather than a job; a later promotion job would be a new story | B-P4-06 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1585 | A publication is recorded as one entry of the local decision-record chain of DP-03 with the record code of a configuration publication, the three version labels, the effective date, the reason, the note, the publishing role code, the version superseded and the time, and the actor is held as a reference and never as a name, so no entry and no event carries a person. | No source gives the record code of a configuration publication, and the decision-record fields DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 carry references and no person field, while NFR-040 and Principle 5 forbid personal data in a shared record. | Append one entry per publication in the transaction that writes the dates, key it by versionId for the event, and carry role codes, labels, dates and reasons only. | GAP-0872 | RWB-P4-E8012-CON sections 1, 8, 11, 12.3, 17; RWB-P4-E8012-APP sections 1, 8, 12.3 | Medium | Decision-record library owner and the data steward before the operations are frozen | Fixes the entry content and the event payload; keeps personal data out of rwb.decision-record.v1 and rwb.access.events.v1 | B-P4-06 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1586 | The QA sample is a three-part consistency check on the rule version recorded on each decision and on that version's rule row, and the service never re-evaluates a package. | The legacy criterion says 'tests each against the rule version that was in force' and the FSD repeats it, but no source says what the test is; the key's pattern list carries no DP-04 and no DP-08, so a Drools re-run is neither in scope nor possible. | For each sampled decision the service reads the rule version recorded on it through the P7 rule-model read and checks that its valid_from and valid_to cover the decision's decided_at, that the recorded rule_id is present in that version's rule_row set, and that the recorded answer agrees with that row's action_text and outputs; each item is PASS or FAIL with one reason code, and no package is evaluated, no KieBase is built and no decision is rewritten. | GAP-0873 | RWB-P4-E8013-APP sections 1, 3, 4, 8 (BR5, BR7), 12.2, 13, 17; RWB-P4-E8013-CON sections 7 (AC3), 8 (BR4), 11, 12.2 | Medium | Confirm with the solution architect and the rwb-decision tech lead that the consistency reading is the target meaning, and with Internal audit that a FAIL verdict is an observation and not a re-decision. | If the reading is rejected the story becomes a DP-04 story with an embedded Drools kit, a local package cache and a rule evaluator call, and its metadata, its dependencies and its test cases all change. | B-P4-06 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1587 | The default and maximum sample size, the period bounds, the page bounds, the draw rule and the reason-code set are parameter rows of rwb-case read through DP-06, never constants in code. | FSD P4 v3 A2.24.3.1 BR-P4-024 says no value a business person may change is written in code, and the legacy story names no size, no bound and no code. | The parameters read of GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters answers the default and maximum sample size, the period bounds, the page bounds, the draw rule and the reason-code set at the version in force; a value outside its bound is a 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and a code outside the set is a configuration error and not a silent pass. | GAP-0873 | RWB-P4-E8013-APP sections 3, 4, 5, 8 (BR6, BR10, BR11), 12.2, 13; RWB-P4-E8013-CON sections 7 (AC2, AC3), 11, 12.2 | Medium | Confirm with the rwb-case owner that the parameter rows exist and are versioned, and with the conduct and QA officer that the sample size and the period bounds are business values and not design values. | If a bound or a code is fixed in code, a change of sampling policy needs a release and the FSD measure of rule and limit changes without a code release cannot be met. | B-P4-06 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1588 | The run's entry is a DP-03 record carrying the run id, the period, the requested and drawn sizes, the passed and failed counts, the window and the reason code of each failure, with no person and no case narrative in it. | The legacy criterion requires the result to be written to the decision log with the rule version and NFR-040 limits each screen and each consumer to the personal data it needs, while no source states the field set of the run entry. | One entry is appended to the local decision-record chain of the DP-03 library in the transaction that stores the answer and the stored items, it is hash-linked through prev_hash and entry_hash, it carries codes, counts, a window and times and no name, no e-mail address, no user reference and no case narrative, and the item set of the run is stored with it so a read never re-draws. | GAP-0873 | RWB-P4-E8013-APP sections 1, 8 (BR8, BR9, BR13), 11, 12.3, 13, 17; RWB-P4-E8013-CON sections 7 (AC2), 11, 12.3, 12.7 | Medium | Confirm with the decision-record library owner and with Internal audit that the counts and the per-failure reason codes are sufficient evidence of a run, and that no case narrative is needed in the record. | If a narrative or a per-case outcome is required in the entry, the record grows a personal-data field, the NFR-040 review applies and the entry schema of the library is amended. | B-P4-06 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-1589 | The data subject request is a register held as decisions of the local decision-record chain of DP-03, with a record code of a data subject request and no new table, and it is served by four operations on /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/data-subject-requests: the open, the decision under If-Match, the read by id and the paged list. | No source declares an operation, a schema, a state set, a record code or a person-reference shape for the capability, and a table of its own would be a second lifecycle beside the append-only chain. | FSD P4 v3 A2.27; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and T-A.1; Architecture v5 slides 14, 41 and 42; ADR-022; the ownership map (no data subject request table) | GAP-0874 | RWB-P4-E8016-APP sections 1, 4, 7, 8, 9, 12; RWB-P4-E8016-CON sections 4, 7, 11, 12 | Medium | Compliance and PDPA officer, solution architect and the decision-record library owner, before the contract baseline is tagged | If a table is preferred, the register read, the state derivation and the four operations change and the contract gains a storage section; the criteria and the rights do not change | B-P4-07 | Unconfirmed (business decision pending) |
| ASM-1590 | The statutory period is a parameter row of rwb-case read through DP-06 at its version in force, its name, value and unit are set by Compliance before the story is Done, and this story computes the due date as calendar days from the received date with no working-day rule; the test fixtures use synthetic periods of 45 and 60 days at versions 2027.1 and 2027.2. | NFR-043 states the target as the statutory period, not set as a working service level, with the status Open, DL26, and no source gives a length, a unit or a working-day rule. | Program BRD v4 NFR-043; TSD P4 v3 T7; DP-06; FSD P4 v3 A2.27.1 | GAP-0875 | RWB-P4-E8016-APP sections 1, 3, 4, 7, 8, 11, 12.2, 13; RWB-P4-E8016-CON sections 3, 7, 11, 12.2 | Medium | Compliance and PDPA officer, with the rwb-case parameters owner, when DL26 is closed | A change of the period is a parameter row and needs no build; a working-day rule would add one calculation and one test | B-P4-07 | Unconfirmed (business decision pending) |

| ASM-1716 | The access-review requester is two activities on task queue `rwb-access` named `buildAccessReviewFile(reviewDate)` and `requestFileDelivery(manifest)`, called by the JOB-18 workflow of RWB-P4-AD008-APP. `buildAccessReviewFile` takes the review date, the starter identity and the feature switch, and returns the manifest plus the rwb-document document ID; the manifest carries the file name, the sha256, the record count, the business date, the interface ID, the requesting service `rwb-access` and the idempotency key `<interfaceId>:<businessDate>`. `requestFileDelivery` takes that manifest and returns the outbound item reference, the item status and the key, and stores the key in the `idempotency_key` object the platform library creates in `rwb_access`, so exactly one request exists per business date. The workflow, its workflow ID and the six-monthly Schedule stay with RWB-P4-AD008-APP, and the rwb-integration login name and the rwb-access login name are written as 'the rwb-access login (DP-02)' until the platform DB story fixes them. | No source names a requester-side activity, its inputs and outputs, the manifest of a requesting service or the key format: Architecture v5 gives P2 the deliverFile activity and the manifest of four elements only, and the legacy story has no requester at all. Every place where a literal interface ID, pattern, layout, recipient or alert target would otherwise appear carries the R9 placeholder 'Not specified in the source documents (CG-B-P4-13-E1007-1; ASM-B-P4-13-E1007-2)', and no value is invented. | Architecture v5 slide 44 names the JOB-18 job and its owner but no interface, no pattern, no layout and no recipient, and no FSD, TSD or legacy section supplies them.
