| ASM-1725 | The local decision-record table is created in rwb_access as decision_record with the entry fields of DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 and the five columns the Work Package names, chain_seq bigint not null unique, prev_hash char(64) not null, entry_hash char(64) not null, corrects_entry_id uuid referencing decision_record (id) and actor_user_id uuid; the canonical form is the legacy BR4 rule (JSON with keys in alphabetical order, UTF-8, no spaces, timestamps in ISO 8601 UTC with microseconds, numbers as strings, empty fields as null) implemented once in CanonicalEntryForm; the genesis prev_hash is 64 zeros held as configuration; the chain lock is a PostgreSQL advisory lock on a per-service chain key; and the database login is named 'the rwb-access login (DP-02)' until the platform DB story fixes it. | The Work Package fixes the five columns, the table name and the genesis value but no source publishes the rest of the column set, the canonical form for a per-service object, the lock key or the login, and the story cannot be built or tested on an empty definition. | Architecture v5 slides 20, 28 and 41; Temporal and Drools Design slide 16; TSD P4 T3.1 and T3.0; Legacy RWB-E1-008 sections 4, 8 BR3 and BR4, 11 and 13; DP-02, DP-03, DP-15 | GAP-0984 | Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 5, 6 and 7; section 8 BR3 and BR4; section 11 Data; section 12.7 Tables owned; section 13 Database and migrations and Configuration and reference data | Medium | Solution architect, the rwb-access tech lead and the platform library owner when RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published | A different column set or canonical form changes the migration, the store, the verifier and the golden vectors; the append-only rule, the chain order, the genesis value and the messages stay as specified. | B-P4-13 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |

| ASM-2507 | The coverage floor of the unit and component gate, the duplication limit and the severity cut-off of static analysis are values of the gate-set version and have no value in the source set; a change to any of them is a reviewed change of the gate set that produces the next version, so a service story and a service repository never carry a threshold of their own. Until the values are published the gate set carries them as named keys with no default in code. | NFR-054 requires the pipeline to block a change that carries a secret, personal data or an unapproved dependency, and Arch v5 slides 11, 20 and 29 require contract tests and the boundary test in every build, but no source gives a coverage floor, a duplication limit or a severity cut-off; a gate that compares against nothing cannot fail a build, and a per-service number would break the one-gate-set rule of this story. | Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11 (contract tests in every build; typed activity contracts), 20 (every service from the service template and the shared libraries; /health and /metrics), 29 (the boundary test fails on a cross-schema reference and is checked in every build), 35 (DevSecOps and supply chain under NIST SP 800-204C and 800-204D), 38 (service template, one Helm chart and golden pipeline as the wave-0 enabler) and 47 (risk "Schema rules broken over time" mitigated by the boundary test in every build); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 NFR-052 and NFR-054; _work/msr/plan/legacy_index.json NF-05 entry (title only); Template and Rules v1 R7.3 and R9; no coverage floor, duplication limit or severity cut-off in any source read | GAP-1428 | Section 3 Preconditions; section 8 BR2; section 11 Data; section 13 Solution plan and Done when; section 16 TC-PLT-NF05-OPS-02 | Medium | Solution architect and the QA lead, with the security architect for the static-analysis cut-off, at the gate-set review before wave 0 exits | The thresholds are changed as values of the gate-set version with no code change and no story change; if a different number is agreed later, the gate set gains one version and every build record keeps the version it ran under. | B-PLT-TPL-02 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |

| ASM-2509 | An exception is recorded with its gate, service, commit or image digest, owner role, reason, expiry date and approver role, and the pipeline expires it into a failure on its expiry date with no further action and no renewal without a new recorded exception; the length of the box, the approver role and the set of gates marked non-waivable are values of the gate set. Rewriting the six paths with a complete register set keeps every value and every criterion of the key, fixes the citation set, and leaves one owner for the slice in this wave. | _work/msr/wp/B-P10-02.md and _work/msr/wp/B2-P10-005.md (the same six output paths); _work/msr/logs/B-P10-02-E2031.asm.jsonl and B-P10-02-E2031.gaps.jsonl (the 25 defaults and 3 gap rows of the earlier draft); _work/msr/gaps/B-P10-02-E2031.part.jsonl and _work/msr/assumptions/B-P10-02-E2031.part.jsonl (13 of the 25 merged); the three story files and three fragments, checked for the R8.1 header, a D-RCV-60 change-log row with the tool line, the 20 metadata rows in the R7.1 order, the 19 section headings in order, the AC origin tags, the R7.2 Level column, tables 12.1 to 12.9 and every CG/ASM citation; Template and Rules v1 sections R7 and R9; root AGENTS.md rules 1, 8, 9 and 12 | GAP-2201 | B2-P10-005: the three story files and the three fragments re-cited and written at their WP paths; _work/msr/gaps/B2-P10-005.jsonl (4 rows); _work/msr/assumptions/B2-P10-005.jsonl (25 rows); _work/msr/editlog/B2-P10-005.md | High | Delivery lead and the stage B2 coordinator at the wave 2 batch close, when the duplicate Work Package is de-duplicated and the B-P10-02 part rows are marked superseded | If the coordinator instead keeps the B-P10-02 set for this key, the six paths must be restored to the earlier draft and the 12 orphan citations of the contract and deployment stories must be settled by adding rows 14 to 25 to _work/msr/assumptions/B-P10-02-E2031.part.jsonl; the two sets carry the same defaults and must not both be numbered at step D1. | B2-P10-005 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-3616 | rwb-case reads the account dates of a case at GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/accounts/{accountId} on the rwb-source-data contract, returning contract date, last payment date and data as of, and the non-working days at GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/calendar/holidays?from={from}&to={to}, both one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retry once with jitter and a breaker per downstream, and it reads no v_ace_* view itself. | The prescription date and the working-day count need another service's data, and no source publishes the account-date read of a set of linked accounts or any holiday read, so the consumed rows, the fake and the AC3 and AC6 mocks need a default. | Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8 and 10; legacy RWB-E1-028 section 12 (RecoveryDataQuery); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-05 and DP-11 | GAP-2202 | RWB-P3-E1028-APP 3, 12.2, 12.8, flow steps 4 and 5; RWB-P3-E1028-CON 12.2 and AC3; RWB-P3-E1028-OPS 12.2 | Medium | Solution architect with the P1 owner in the baseline review of RWB-P3-E1028-CON. | If P1 publishes another path or another shape, one consumed row, the AccountDatesClient and CalendarClient adapters and two fakes change; no schema, event or workflow change. | B2-P3-001 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-3617 | The stage-clock pause arrives as rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1 and rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1 on rwb.deviation.events.v1 from S8 in wave 2; at wave 1 the same pause and resume are reachable through the P3 case action contract, and AC10 is proved against the rwb-deviation contract mock until S8 exists. | AC10 is owned by this story and the deviation service is wave 2 while the assigned dependency set carries no S8 contract story, so the story needs one stated path for each wave. | RWB-ITG-E1028-ITG section 12.2 and flow step 11; Architecture v5 slide 42 (event 06 and 07); Template and Rules R5.4 | GAP-2202 | RWB-P3-E1028-APP 3, 4 (step 9), 12.4, 12.8; RWB-P3-E1028-CON 12.4 and AC5; RWB-P3-E1028-OPS 12.4 | Medium | Solution architect with the S8 owner and the wave 1 harness owner before the story's Done. | If S8 publishes another event name or another key, one consumed row, the DeviationSignalRouter and one fixture change; the prescription clock is unaffected in every case. | B2-P3-001 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-3618 | The Timer resource carries escalatedToRole as an optional role code of up to 30 characters and escalatedAt as an optional date-time, both written by the timer story and mapped to timer.escalated_to_role and timer.escalated_at; the rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1 payload carries caseId, caseNo, timerId, timerType, expiresAt and escalateTo with caseId as the key and no personal data, and both are additive within major version 1. | The TSD timer table and the logical model have no row for the two escalation values and the catalogue gives no payload field list, so the baseline cannot publish a schema without a default. | TSD P3 v3 T3.1; legacy RWB-E1-028 section 12 (TimerBreached EV-19); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42; RWB-P3-E2015-APP section 11 | GAP-2203 | RWB-P3-E1028-CON 12.1, 12.3, 11 and AC1, AC2, AC6; RWB-P3-E1028-APP 12.1, 12.3 | Medium | Solution architect and the data steward in the baseline review, and the P7 owner for the record reference. | A type, length or payload change is one schema change inside major version 1 and one regenerated type set; no table, event topic or workflow change. | B2-P3-001 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-3619 | The four operational values are provisional until UAT: the worker-poll alert fires when no poll of rwb-case is seen for 2 minutes, the catch-up alert fires when a timer stayed unmet 10 minutes after the worker returned, TimerBreached volume alerts when the hourly count leaves the trailing 7-day band by more than 3 times, and the MSG-P7-003 rate alerts above 1% of timer fires over 15 minutes. | The deployment cannot ship without a poll window, a catch-up window, a band and a rate, and no source gives any of them; each stays a values-file entry and never code. | Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 28 and 44; legacy RWB-E1-028 sections 5, 13 and 17; Template and Rules R7.2 s17 | GAP-2204 | RWB-P3-E1028-OPS 11, 13 (alert mapping) and 14 | Medium | DevOps lead with the rwb-case service owner at UAT, and the platform observability owner for the band definition. | A threshold change is a values-file change and one runbook line; no code, contract or schema change. | B2-P3-001 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-3620 | rwb-reporting builds the queue, ageing and breach measures from the events into its own projection (CaseTransferred, CaseAllocated, CaseStateChanged, TimerBreached and the decision record), and rwb-case publishes no measure feed and writes no file; the nightly lake copy of JOB-15 and the INT-19 and INT-20 outbound batch are removed under DP-17. | The legacy publication of the measure snapshot was the JOB-15 copy to the data lake for Power BI, and Arch v5 removes the data lake and both interfaces, so the story needs one stated replacement for the published measures of REQ-RDF-012. | RWB-E1-030 sections 3, 4 step 9 and 12; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 row JOB-15; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 8 ('Data lake / Power BI not connected (INT-19/20 removed)'); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-17 | GAP-2205 | RWB-P3-E1030-APP 1, 2, 4 (step 11), 12.3, 12.9, 17; RWB-P3-E1030-CON 5 (C6), 8 (BR7), 12.3; RWB-P3-E1030-OPS 8 (BR9), 12.9, 17 | Medium | Solution architect with the rwb-reporting owner at the baseline review of RWB-P3-E1030-CON and in the wave 1 verification loop. | If reporting needs a published measure read instead of a projection, one operation is added to RWB-P3-E1030-CON and one controller to RWB-P3-E1030-APP; the snapshot table, its status and the reconciliation rule do not change. | B2-P3-002 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-3621 | MSG-P3-028, MSG-P3-011 and MSG-P3-029 are delivered at wave 1 on the ACE notification path with their message ID as the template key, as the monolith did, and move to rwb-comms when P6 lands; the story consumes no contract of a notice service. | The legacy notifier sent the three messages through the monolith's notification path and no source assigns a notice contract to this key, so the alert rows of section 14 need one stated delivery path that adds no contract dependency. | RWB-E1-030 section 4 steps 4, 7 and 10 and section 14; FSD P3 v4 'Existing capability check' row 'Notification path / REUSE / ACE notification path'; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8 and 10 | GAP-2205 | RWB-P3-E1030-APP 3, 4 (steps 5, 8, 9), 14; RWB-P3-E1030-CON 12.9 and 14; RWB-P3-E1030-OPS 5 and 14 | Medium | Solution architect with the rwb-comms owner and the platform notification owner before the story's Done. | If the messages move to rwb-comms at wave 1, one consumed contract row and one adapter appear in RWB-P3-E1030-APP and the C dependency is added; no AC, no message text and no snapshot field changes. | B2-P3-002 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-3622 | The run record of a business date is the Temporal record of the DailyCaseRun run (its activity results name the moves and any case that stayed with MSG-P7-003), and the legacy rerun call is replaced by triggering the Schedule rwb-case-rebalance-daily by hand under Platform administration U, with no REST operation published; a consumer reads a date's moves through GET /cases with the queue filter and the snapshot through GET /queues. | The legacy job table, the job monitor and the rerun endpoint were Quartz artifacts of the monolith; the Schedule replaces the job trigger and the ownership map publishes no jobs or run-record operation, so the run record and the rerun surface need one stated default. | RWB-E1-030 sections 4 step 1, 5 (X4) and 12 (job table and rerun endpoint); Batch and Scheduling Design v4 row JOB-06; _work/msr/context/P3.md REST rows; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-10 | GAP-2205 | RWB-P3-E1030-APP 4 (step 1 and 6), 5 (X4, X8), 10, 12.5; RWB-P3-E1030-CON 5 (C5), 11, 12.5; RWB-P3-E1030-OPS 4 (step 3), 9, 10 | Medium | Solution architect with the workflow platform owner and the RW-PLATADM owner before the story's Done. | If a published run record or rerun operation is required, one operation and one table row appear in the contract and one controller in the build story; the moves, the snapshot and the ACs do not change. | B2-P3-002 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-3623 | The Schedule fires at 06:30 in the bank's business time zone held as a value in the values file (assumed Asia/Bangkok until the business owner confirms it), with an overlap policy of skip and a catch-up window held as a value; replica counts, resource limits, the ingress host, the alert thresholds and the activity retry values are values in the same file with no default chosen by this story. | The chart and the Schedule must be renderable in SIT and UAT, and no source gives a zone, a catch-up window, a replica count or an alert threshold, so the story needs one stated set of value names without inventing the numbers. | Batch and Scheduling Design v4 row JOB-06 (Daily 06:30); RWB-E1-030 section 13; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8 and 44; Template and Rules R1 U7 (dates and times copied, values not invented) | GAP-2207 | RWB-P3-E1030-OPS 3, 4, 8, 9, 11; RWB-P3-E1030-APP 12.6; RWB-P3-E1030-CON 12.6 | Medium | DevOps lead with the business owner and the workflow platform team at the SIT dry run. | If the zone or the catch-up window differs, one values key changes per environment and the runbook state table changes; no code, no schema and no AC changes. | B2-P3-002 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-3624 | The team filter is an optional additive query parameter on GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases, combined with the other filters by AND inside the caller's scope, and it is published in the baseline as an addition to the request list of API-P3-001; the export operation keeps the team parameter it already lists in API-P3-017. | The legacy flow, scenario AC1 and FSD A2.19 filter by queue, team and status, the legacy section 12 adds the team parameter, and the technical specification lists it for the export only, so the list operation needs one stated answer; and it stays optional so no existing consumer breaks. | Legacy RWB-E1-031 sections 4 and 12; TSD P3 v3 T-A.2 API-P3-001 and API-P3-017; FSD P3 v4 A2.19; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-11 | GAP-2208 | RWB-P3-E1031-APP 3, 7 (AC1), 8 BR2, 12.1; RWB-P3-E1031-CON 4 step 3, 7 AC3, 12.1 | Medium | Solution architect with the gateway-bff owner in the baseline review of RWB-P3-E1031-CON. | If the team parameter is refused on the list, one query parameter, one filter control and AC1 of the flow change; no schema, event or workflow change. | B2-P3-003 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |

| ASM-3626 | The access-log entry is written through the rwb-access access-log operation of RWB-P4-E1039-CON at POST /api/recovery/access/v1/access-events, one hop with a 2 s timeout and no retry on the export path, carrying eventCode AC-EXPT with the actor user reference, the time, the area Case record, the right R, the filter set and the row count; a failure answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 and no file is made, and the 401 and 403 texts are the rwb-access ones. | The legacy story names the Java interface AccessEventPublisher and its fields but no operation, and the split moves the access log to rwb-access, so the consumed row, its fake and the refusal of AC5 need one stated surface. | Legacy RWB-E1-031 sections 4 step 7, 5 (X3), 12 and 14; Architecture v5 slide 8 (access and PII logging in ACE Common, access service P4); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-11 | GAP-2208 | RWB-P3-E1031-APP 3, 4 steps 8 and 9, 7 (AC2, AC5), 12.2, 12.8, 14; RWB-P3-E1031-CON 7 AC7, 12.2, 14 | Medium | P4 owner of rwb-access in the baseline review of RWB-P4-E1039-CON, with the rwb-case service owner. | If the operation path or the field set differs, one consumed row, the AccessEventClient adapter, one fake and the AC2 assertion change; no case data and no event topic change. | B2-P3-003 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |

| ASM-3628 | caselist.export.maxrows stays 10,000 as a parameter row with the version in force, the page-size default 50 and maximum 200 stay the parameter rows of RWB-P3-E2011-APP, and the rwb-case login name is taken from the platform naming rule at deployment rather than fixed in this story. | The legacy story assumes 10,000 under DL11 and gives no page bounds, the queue-view story publishes the bounds, and the per-service login has no name in any source, so each value needs one stated home. | Legacy RWB-E1-031 sections 3, 8 BR5 and 13; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-02, DP-06; context pack P3 (schema rwb_case, one login per service) | GAP-2208 | RWB-P3-E1031-APP 3, 11, 13; RWB-P3-E1031-CON 12.7 | Medium | Business owner for the row limit at UAT, and the platform DB owner for the login name. | A limit or page-bound change is a parameter row change; a login change is a deployment value; no code, contract or schema change. | B2-P3-003 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |

| ASM-3632 | The case state change and the creation item of the timeline are read as the decision records of the case, in time order, from the decision-record query of rwb-decision; rwb-case adds no status-history table and keeps no second copy of the history, and the creation of a case is its first decision record, which carries the entry rule and its version. | The legacy story read its own module's decision_log_entry and showed a status-change item and a creation item, but no P3 table holds a case status history and the decision record now lives with P7, so the story and the contract need one stated source. | Legacy RWB-E1-035 sections 4, 11 and 12; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 (assignment and recovery_case); context pack P3 ownership rows (15 tables); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-03 | GAP-2210 | RWB-P3-E1035-APP 1, 3, 4 (steps 4 and 5), 8 BR9, 11, 12.2, 12.5, 12.7; RWB-P3-E1035-CON 11, 12.2 | Medium | Solution architect with the P7 owner in the baseline review of RWB-P3-E1035-CON. | If P7 brings its own case-event query or a status history is added later, one consumed row, the DecisionRecordClient mapping and two mocks change; no schema, event or workflow change. | B2-P3-004 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-3633 | A transfer item takes its to queue from assignment.queue_id (DF-WRK-039) and its reason code from assignment.transfer_reason_code (DF-WRK-040), and its from queue and from owner from the closed previous assignment row of the same case (ended_at set), with the queue codes resolved on the queue table of rwb_case; the rule ID comes from assignment.rule_id (DF-WRK-016) and the rule version from the decision record of the transfer, never from a column. | AC2 and the legacy section 12 show the from and to queue and owner plus the rule version of a transfer, but assignment has no from-queue column and no rule-version column, so the detail needs a stated derivation that invents no field. | TSD P3 v3 T3.1 assignment DF-WRK-009 to DF-WRK-040; legacy RWB-E1-035 sections 11 and 12; legacy RWB-E1-021 transfer with reason; context pack P3 tables (assignment, queue) | GAP-2210 | RWB-P3-E1035-APP 5 (X9), 8 BR8, 11, 13 (build step 1); RWB-P3-E1035-CON 11 | Medium | Solution architect with the P3 owner and the P7 owner at the baseline review, before TC-E1-035-02 is signed off. | A dedicated from-queue column later is one additive column and one mapper line; the item shape and the AC are unchanged. | B2-P3-004 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |

| ASM-3688 | RWB-E1-011 is split four ways in the target: rwb-source-data owns the enterprise run ReconciliationWorkflow, reconciliation_result, REC-01's account count and balance, REC-02 and the case-list publish gate; rwb-case owns the case-side facts - the exclusion list of REC-01, the plan link of REC-03 and the referential check of REC-05 over recovery_case, case_account, case_party and case_entry_exclusion; rwb-asset and rwb-comms own their own referential slices; rwb-ITG proves the whole of JOB-04 end to end. The rwb-case slice writes no row of reconciliation_result, owns no legacy acceptance criterion, and treats the platform CONs of its DP table (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON) and its own contracts RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON as present before the wave-1 build rather than as build dependencies, so Depends on (build) and Contract dependencies stay None as the plan sets them. | The plan gives a secondary rwb-case slice of the key with empty H, C, I and X lists and no legacy criterion, while the legacy story is a single shared JOB-04 step and no source draws the boundary; without a ruling the story cannot be scoped, its tables cannot be placed and the lane cannot be cut. | Legacy RWB-E1-011 sections 1, 2, 12; WP B2-P3-014 story line; RWB-P1-E1011-APP sections 1, 12.7 and 19; FSD P3 v4 A2.5, AC-EXC-P3-027-03, AC-EXC-P3-028-01, AC-EXC-P3-034-03; Template and Rules R5.4, R5.7, R6 | GAP-2232 | RWB-P3-E1011-APP sections 1, 2, 3, 7, 12.7, 18 and 19; fragment RWB-P3-E1011-APP H, C, I, X | Medium | Solution architect with the rwb-case and rwb-source-data service owners in the baseline review of the P3 story set. | If the boundary moves, one precondition, the criteria set and the tables of section 12.7 change; no operation, event or workflow of this story changes. | B2-P3-014 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-3689 | The case-side run writes its own tables in schema rwb_case - case_quality_run (unique business_date), case_quality_result (unique rec_code, quality_check, business_date, product_group, with the legacy reconciliation_result column names of DF-OPS-118 to DF-OPS-129) and case_quality_break (index on business_date together with rec_code, and on key_type together with key_value) - created by V1011_1__case_quality.sql in the per-service Flyway sequence; the three check names are EXCL under REC-01, PLAN under REC-03 and KEY under REC-05, the result values are PASS, BREAK and not run, and reconciliation_result itself stays rwb-source-data's table and is never written or read here. | The legacy result table belongs to another service in the target and the case slice needs a durable result, a run record and a break list, but no source names them or their keys. | Legacy RWB-E1-011 sections 11, 12, 13 and AC1, AC6; RWB-P1-E1011-APP section 12.7; context pack ownership rows (15 P3 tables); TSD P1 v3 reconciliation_result | GAP-2233 | RWB-P3-E1011-APP sections 8, 11, 12.7, 12.8, 13 and 16; fragment RWB-P3-E1011-APP | Medium | Solution architect with the rwb-case service owner and the ACE team in the migration review of V1011_1. | If the tables or the keys are named otherwise, section 11, one row of 12.7, one fake, the migration and the two criteria AC1 and AC6 change; no operation or workflow changes. | B2-P3-014 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-3690 | The case-side run is answered by four operations on /api/recovery/case/v1 - GET /quality-runs/{businessDate} with Platform administration R, GET /quality-results with Platform administration R and Reporting R, GET /reconciliation/status with Platform administration R and the rwb-source-data service identity, and POST /quality-runs/{businessDate}/rerun with Platform administration U and an Idempotency-Key - all read only except the rerun, answering 400, 401, 403, 404, 409 and 503 with the problem body of the rwb-case service contract and never recomputing a variance at the boundary; the run publishes no Kafka record, because the case event catalogue carries no reconciliation event, and the run record goes to the local decision record instead. | AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5, AC7 and TC-E1-011-07 read and restart a run that the legacy story exposed through a job listing and a scheduler console, and no source gives the target operations, rights or response shapes. | Legacy RWB-E1-011 sections 10 and 12; TSD P3 v3 API-P3-001 to API-P3-027; context pack REST operations and events; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-03, DP-11, DP-13, DP-14 | GAP-2234 | RWB-P3-E1011-APP sections 10, 12.1, 12.3, 12.8, 13 and 16; fragment RWB-P3-E1011-APP ops_provided and events_published | Medium | Solution architect with the gateway-bff owner and the rwb-case service owner before the story's Done. | If the paths, the rights or the error set land otherwise, section 12.1, one fake, the access test and one build step change; no table or workflow changes. | B2-P3-014 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-3691 | The ACE side of every case-side check arrives through the rwb-source-data contract and never through a recovery.v_ace_* view: the freshness read GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness answers COMPLETE or STALE with the last complete business date per data product, and one product-coded records read per data product answers the rows of the business date in force - account key, days past due and balance for the accounts product, person key for the customer product, and plan reference, booked date and plan status for the plans product, which is the plan side of REC-03 and REC-05 for a recovery_case.plan_ref. Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout, one GET retry with jitter and a breaker, and is faked from Day 1. | The legacy story reads six ACE views directly and the target gives the views to rwb-source-data alone, so the checks of AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4 and AC7 cannot run without a read shape for the accounts, customer and plan rows, and no source states it. | Legacy RWB-E1-011 sections 3, 4 and 11; context pack naming rules and DP-05; Architecture v5 slides 8 and 29 as repeated in the context pack; FSD P3 v4 A2.5.3.2 | GAP-2235 | RWB-P3-E1011-APP sections 3, 4, 11, 12.2, 12.8 and 13; fragment RWB-P3-E1011-APP ops_consumed | Medium | Solution architect with the rwb-source-data service owner before the story's Done. | If the contract publishes other paths or elements, four rows of 12.2, four fakes, one criterion and one activity change; no table changes. | B2-P3-014 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-3692 | The case service never writes the case list: it answers GET /api/recovery/case/v1/reconciliation/status for a business date with RELEASED, HELD or NOT_RUN and the count of unexplained exclusions per product group, and the case-list gate of rwb-source-data reads that answer before it releases the case list. A break or an incomplete data product therefore holds the case list of the date through that answer, and the rerun of AC5 is the only path that releases it. | AC2 and AC4 keep the legacy behaviour of holding the case list and case_list_row.publish_status is rwb-source-data's table in the target, so the verdict must cross the service boundary in a named shape that no source gives. | Legacy RWB-E1-011 section 4 steps 3 and 10, section 12 (excludedAccountsByProduct); RWB-P1-E1011-APP sections 12.2 and 13; Template and Rules R5.4 and R5.5 DP-11 | GAP-2236 | RWB-P3-E1011-APP sections 5, 8 (BR7), 9, 12.1, 12.2 and 16; fragment RWB-P3-E1011-APP ops_provided | Medium | Solution architect with the rwb-source-data service owner in the baseline review of the two slices. | If the gate consumes an event or calls another operation, one row of 12.1, one row of 12.3 and one criterion change; no table changes. | B2-P3-014 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |

| ASM-3769 | A configuration rollback of rwb-access moves the four tables of this service that carry a version label of their own: permission by matrix_version, masking_rule by masking_version, role_conflict by conflict_version and delegation_limit by limit_version. It is a state and date change on the rows already stored and never a copy: the withdrawn rows go to ROLLED_BACK with valid_to yesterday (is_active false and state ROLLED_BACK for permission, which has no date column) and the restored rows go to IN_FORCE with valid_to null, so every row keeps its id. The version before the named one is the label that was in force immediately before it in the same table, read by valid_from for the three dated tables and by the label order fixed at the contract review for permission. The role list carries no version column in TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and no role row is moved. | ASM-3814 | An incident of rwb-access is a record and not a table: one entry of the local decision-record chain of DP-03 for the open, carrying the steps DETECTED and HELD, and one entry for the closure, carrying the steps FIXED, RECORDED and REPORTED, each written in the same transaction as its idempotency row. The state is derived from the entries - OPEN after the first and CLOSED after the second - and is never stored. The incident id is minted by this service and is opaque to every consumer. The three operations are POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/incidents, POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/incidents/{incidentId}/closure and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/incidents/{incidentId}, and the incident surface is composed at the edge by the gateway-bff route because no source names an incident screen. The detection signal stays with RWB-PLT-OBS: the reference and the detection time are entered on the surface, because TSD P4 v3 T5.1 declares no interface from the observability platform to P4. | No source contains an incident entity, an incident operation or an incident screen, and the monolith kept the path inside one administration process, so the record, the paths, the state model and the composition of the surface have to be fixed before the story can be built; leaving them open would stop the wave and inviting the record into a new table of this service would add a table the ownership map does not have. | Legacy RWB-E8-017 (story statement, AC1 detect hold fix record report, screens SCR-39 and SCR-41); FSD P4 v3 A2.28.1 to A2.28.3 and A2.28.4; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (five P4 tables), T5.1 (INT-21 and INT-22 only), T6.1 and appendix T-A.1; the context pack rows for P4 (four REST operations, no event, JOB-18); DP-03 and DP-19; Template and Rules R5.7 Day-1 rule. | GAP-2301 | RWB-P4-E8017-APP sections 1, 3, 4, 7 (AC3), 8 (BR1, BR2, BR5), 9, 11, 12.1, 12.4, 12.7, 13, 15; RWB-P4-E8017-CON sections 1, 7 (AC2, AC3), 8 (BR5, BR7), 11, 12.1, 12.7 | Medium | Solution architect, the tech lead of rwb-access and the owner of the decision-record library at the contract review of RWB-P4-E8017-CON | If the edition of an incident must be a table of its own, the ownership map gains a table, the Flyway story of this service changes and the read becomes a query rather than a chain read; the step set, the states and the three paths do not change. | B2-P4-017 | Confirmed (programme directive, 26 November 2026) |
| ASM-3815 | The incident path is authorised by the Platform administration letters of TSD P4 v3 T6.1: C on the open, U on the closure and R on the read, held by RW-PLATADM as CRUD, RW-SECADM as CRUDA, RW-AUDIT and RW-COE as R and by the case roles as a dash. The legacy permission table of RWB-E8-017, which gives Rules and parameters C to RW-COE and A to RW-RISK, is the rule-change right set of the same chapter and not this feature's; R-PREC puts the Technical Specifications above the story master. A caller without the letter is refused 403 with MSG-P4-002, and a caller holding a dash in every held area is answered 404 with MSG-P4-003 on the read.
